items.text: As a regional legislator, voted for that year's regional health budget law, which raised public health coverage spending by about 4 percent and reversed a proposed funding cut for safety-net hospitals.

As a regional legislator, voted for the following year's regional health budget law, which raised payment rates for health providers but did not fund continued coverage for the roughly 2 percent of residents set to lose a regional low-income health plan after the national budget law's cuts, a share taken from a news estimate.
As a regional legislator, cosponsored a bill to create a single public health plan for every resident of the region, paid for through a payroll assessment.
Said they would push in the national legislature for a single public health plan for every resident, alongside organizing outside it to pass one.
Ran on a platform of guaranteed paid family and medical leave, a guaranteed public job, and expanded unemployment benefits.
